items.title: Percy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Kenny Dorham too? [INTERVIEWEE] And some of Milt Jackson’s dates, and that was how I paid my rent making record dates.

ctx.x: No, it was with Johnny Hodges and Sonny Greer. Boy, we had a good time on that gig. That was the only time I played with the Duke Ellington guys. But during that period, like becoming a house bass player, so to speak, for Blue Note and Prestige, the jazz labels, I recorded with an awful lot of people, including Monk and Miles and this discography, I can’t even recall who I recorded with. It was Horace Silver’s first date…
And some of Milt Jackson’s dates, and that was how I paid my rent making record dates. I think it was about $55 a sessions, or something like that, for a three-hour session.
